findings: Desktop controls and the current-schedule card form a readable two-column layout; timezone, start, optional end, end policy and section selection are visible.

Existing-schedule state visibly disables a second open schedule, and calendar captures distinguish saved scene start/end entries.
The mobile empty-month capture keeps filters, month navigation, grid and agenda within the page width.
The full desktop history capture distinguishes current expiry from the earlier no-expiry revision and presents restore-as-draft controls clearly.
Four contact sheets preserve the month, undated, DST, script-free, expiry, review and restored states across both storage modes.
The full desktop Hero editor keeps the canvas, image library, background settings and publishing controls in separate usable regions; the Schedule action and current version/build are visible.
The full footer preview preserves the relative positions and scale of the scene content, custom button and test photo layer.

The reviewed editor and published Hero captures preserve the checkerboard geometry and relative placement of the cyan and magenta test layers.
Desktop and mobile contact sheets retain the expected photo/mask relationships across file and MySQL root and nested cases.
These are intentionally cropped synthetic geometry fixtures; the review does not assert full typography visibility within their cropped scene regions.
The full mobile owner editor keeps reorder controls, text fields, destination controls and the visibility option within the available width.

Owner, header and footer contact sheets retain readable navigation hierarchy, clear expansion controls and visible footer credit.
The expanded mobile custom footer grows in normal page flow and keeps the developer credit above the visible music player.
The full mobile authentication capture places the compact footer at the bottom of the short page with no empty player reservation when that player is omitted.
The short-page and expanded-menu contact sheets preserve footer placement and player clearance in the reviewed file/MySQL cases.
